dataset.name: ESS-DIVE Reporting Format for Comma-separated Values (CSV) File Structure
description: The ESS-DIVE reporting format for Comma-separated Values (CSV) file structure is based on a combination of existing guidelines and recommendations including some found within the Earth Science Community with valuable input from the Environmental Systems Science (ESS) Community. The CSV reporting format is designed to promote interoperability and machine-readability of CSV data files while also facilitating the collection of some file-level metadata content. Tabular data in the form of rows and columns should be archived in its simplest form, and we recommend submitting these tabular data following the ESS-DIVE reporting format for generic comma-separated values (CSV) text format files.

In general, the CSV file format is more likely accessible by future systems when compared to a proprietary format and CSV files are preferred because this format is easier to exchange between different programs increasing the interoperability of a data file. By defining the reporting format and providing guidelines for how to structure CSV files and some field content within, this can increase the machine-readability of the data file for extracting, compiling, and comparing the data across files and systems.

Data package files are in .csv, .png, and .md. Open the .csv with e.g. Microsoft Excel, LibreOffice, or Google Sheets. Open the .md files by downloading and using a text editor (e.g., notepad or TextEdit). Open the .png in e.g. a web browser, photo viewer/editor, or Google Drive.

measurementTechnique: In order to create the CSV reporting format, we compared existing standards and best practices for CSV, spreadsheets, and similar data at relevant agencies both within the United States and internationally. The CSV file format is not standardized and there are many variants with RFC 4180 (Shafranovich 2005) commonly treated as the standard. The BADC-CSV format (Pepler & Parton 2009) is a variant of the CSV file format created by the British Atmospheric Data Centre for atmospheric observation data. The BADC-CSV format (Pepler & Parton 2009) is a variant of the CSV file format created by the British Atmospheric Data Centre for atmospheric observation data. The format requires that the file be self-describing through the implementation of a strict and detailed header. The ASCII format follows RFC 4180, is intuitive, and was created for Earth science data. CSV files are compatible with Unicode and ASCII character sets; however, the EDIrecommends ASCII text (256 characters) delimited by tab or comma (EDI 2019).

We also compared CSV formatted data from select DOE ESS Community research programs. This involved comparing two CSV data files from each program - AmeriFLUX, EDI, HgSFA, NGEEA, NGEET, SPRUCE, WHONDRS. We provide crosswalk within this data package to provide a summary of how these different projects organize and structure their CSV files. Within the crosswalk, the first column is used to order the rows, the second column provides evaluation categories, the third column is a description of how the data files are evaluated, and the following 14 columns are the data file evaluations. The final column provides whether there was a consensus across the file evaluations. The initial research and comparisons contributed to the first draft of a CSV reporting format. Later stages of the draft were used to develop a crosswalk table comparing this CSV reporting format to multiple other guidelines and best practices within DOE and beyond.

We gathered feedback on the various drafts of the CSV reporting format through email solicitations, presentations at multiple meetings, one-on-one sessions, and small group discussions. We interacted with numerous projects/people across the ESS Community and with each interaction improved the CSV reporting format.
Presentations included the ESS-DIVE Community Fund meeting, 2020 ESS Cyberinfrastructure meeting, and ESS-DIVE Monthly webinar. We received detailed feedback from 26 people representing SPRUCE, FACE, NGEE Tropics, Mercury SFA, NASA DAAC, NGEE Arctic, WHONDRS, ESS-DIVE, Joint Global Change Research, SBIR Phase ll Quantitative BioSciences and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory Groundwater Quality SFA, IDEAS Watershed Project, Integrated Coastal Modeling (ICoM), AmeriFlux, Watershed Function SFA, InteRFACE, International Arctic Research Center, and Biogeochemistry of Actinides SFA.
This data package includes a quick guide to the CSV reporting format, detailed guide, a data file example, and crosswalk table.
